correctness.rationale: PASS: Any s-edge induced-star forest on c components in cubic graph of N vertices uses s+c vertices and incident-edge budget 2s+3c≤3N/2; as s≤3c this yields s≤N/2, with equality requiring 6|N. For Heawood N=14 this rules out seven edges; Fano incidence and diameter-three observations classify all six-edge packings as three 2-edge stars centered on the points of one line or the lines through one point, exactly 14. For Desargues N=20 this rules out ten; direct rank-two/rank-three subset-inclusion argument classifies nine-edge packings as 3+2+2+2 stars with all centers in one part and unique full-star center, exactly 20. Independently reconstructed both graphs from F2^3 dot-product incidences and 2-subset/3-subset inclusions, then built edge compatibility by explicit third-edge scans and exhaustively enumerated all maximal compatible sets. Heawood maximal-size histogram {3:14,6:14}, 14 size-six with profile (2,2,2); Desargues {5:132,6:105,8:30,9:20}, 20 size-nine with profile (2,2,2,3). Structural automorphism transitivity follows from Fano duality/collineations and S5 plus complementation; finite enumeration was independent of that orbit argument.

evidence: Universal cubic estimate is N/2, with equality cases; for N=14,20 equality is excluded by simple divisibility.
Neither generic equality characterization nor product/hypercube family statements force sharp lower witnesses or counts 14 and 20.

value.rationale: PASS: The Heawood and Desargues graphs are canonical small cubic bipartite incidence geometries, not arbitrary chosen finite graphs. Both miss the sharp general cubic EOP upper bound by exactly one, and determining all maximum configurations and their automorphism-orbit rigidity refines a natural near-equality problem not settled by scalar universal bounds. Complete two-object finite classifications with concise geometric explanation can be reusable extremal benchmarks.

limitations: Exactly the two specified labeled 14-vertex Heawood and 20-vertex Desargues graphs; 14 and 20 count labeled edge sets, each one symmetry orbit.
